profile.name: Hayase Hina
profile.nature: Talks at double speed, asks three questions per breath, blunt enough to bruise. Hates rumours, fake news and the Ura board; checks every fact twice. Delivers everything into the hand, never through a third person. Remembers every summer she played with Toru as a kid - and is quietly furious that he doesn't. Secretly writes a romance serial online with a hero who looks suspiciously like him.
profile.rumour: Hina from 2-C? She leaves the flower shop at 7:55 on the dot, takes a photo of the same lamp post, and is at school by 8:15. Her mum answers the door. Her mum asks questions back.
profile.mio_says: The newspaper girl leaves at five to eight. She photographs the same lamp post every morning. Something lives in that lamp post, you know. Fufu. She hasn't noticed yet.

wait_outside: The flower shop's shutter is half up. Buckets of hydrangeas wait on the step. Upstairs, someone is talking very fast to nobody.
From the window above the shop: "Where's my roll of film? Mum! Did you move the film? It was IN the fridge!"
A camera shutter clicks upstairs. Then again. Then a frustrated "Overexposed!"
You can hear Hina reading her own article out loud and arguing with it.
Mrs. Hayase is arranging tulips by the door. She smiles at you like she knows a secret.
The radio inside the florist plays the weather. Hina's voice yells over it: "It's going to rain again! It always rains now!"
Upstairs a printer whirrs. "No, no, no - don't jam. Please don't jam. Not today."
A delivery bike leans against the wall, its basket full of paper bags of seeds.
The smell of wet soil and lilies drifts out of the shop. Somebody runs up the stairs, then back down.
Hina's voice: "Mum, do I look like a serious journalist? Don't laugh. DON'T LAUGH."
ring_self_low: The upstairs window slams open. "Who's - oh. Oh! It's YOU. What are you doing here? How do you know where I live? ...Never mind. I know how. Small town."
Hina comes down with a pen in her mouth. "Asagiri. Toru. You. At my door. Is this a story? Is something happening? Tell me everything."
"You rang our bell. Nobody rings, the shop door's always open. Are you lost? You were always getting lost."
"Morning. ...You don't remember this street, do you. Of course you don't."
"Hold on, don't move." Click. She photographs you. "Evidence. Now, why are you here?"
"Hi. I'm not ready. I'm ninety percent ready. The other ten is hair."
"If you're from the Ura board, you can turn round right now." She squints. "...No, you're too dopey for that. Hi."
"Asagiri-kun! Ha. That's weird. I used to call you something else. Never mind. What?"
"Is it about the article? It's not finished. Nobody reads drafts. Not even you."
"You came here on purpose? Wait - let me write that down. 'Day eleven. He came on purpose.'"
ring_self_mid: "Toru! Good, I need a witness. Mum says my glasses are crooked. Are they crooked? Don't lie."
"You're here! Five minutes. Three. Hold my notebook. Don't read it. Don't READ it."
"Morning! You rang twice. You always rang twice when we were kids. ...You don't remember. It's fine."
"Perfect timing, I've got a question for you. I've got eleven questions. Walk and talk?"
"Toru! You came. Okay. Okay okay okay. Let me grab my camera."
"I knew it was you. Who else rings like a delivery man? Dad. Only Dad. And you."
"Come in for a second? Actually no, Mum'll interrogate you. Wait outside. I'll be quick."
"You're early. Good. Early people are trustworthy people. That's a fact. I checked."
"Ah! I haven't done my hair. Don't take a photo. You don't have a camera. Good."
"You came again? I'm writing a theory about this. The theory is: you like me. As a friend. Probably."
ring_self_high: Hina opens the door already grinning. "I was watching from the window. For six minutes. Don't make it weird."
"Toru! I printed you something. It's a photo. Of us. From 2016. You don't have to remember. Just look at it."
"You came! Of course you came. You always come now. I should stop being surprised. I'm still surprised."
"Morning, partner-in-truth! I've got strawberry milk. Two. One's yours. Don't argue."
"Hey. I'm glad it's you. I had a weird dream about running all night. Walking's nicer."
"Look! I fixed the lens. Now I can take photos of you that aren't blurry. Not that I take photos of you. Often."
"You know Mum calls you 'that boy' now? Like there's only one. Ugh. Let's go before she comes out."
"Ready! Notebook, pen, spare pen, spare spare pen, film, you. All here."
"Good morning, Toru." She says it properly, then ruins it. "Okay, that was too formal. Morning! Let's go!"
"I waited at the window like a dog. Don't tell Hayate I said dog. He'll take it personally."
ring_parent: Mrs. Hayase opens the door with an armful of lilies. "Oh! Toru-kun! My, haven't you grown. Hina! HINA! It's that boy!"
"You're the Asagiri boy." The florist beams. "You used to fall asleep in my sunflower bucket. You don't remember? Hina remembers."
"Good morning! Hina's upstairs fighting her hair. Come in, come in. Mind the buckets."
"Oh, it's you! She's been at the window since half past. Don't tell her I said so."
Mrs. Hayase looks you up and down. "Hm. Taller. Still sleepy. Good. HINA, your childhood friend is here!"
"Toru-kun! Here, take a flower. No, not for me, silly. For whoever you walk to school with." She winks. "HINA!"
"Morning, morning! My husband's already gone on his round. Six thirty, every day, in the rain. Hina's nearly ready."
"Ah, Toru-kun. Have you eaten? You haven't. Here, a rice ball. Hina made it. Badly."
"She's checking her article for the fourth time. Sit on the step. The cat there doesn't bite. Mostly."
"Oh dear. You look tired. Are you sleeping? Rain every night, isn't it. HINA, move it!"

ring_parent.t: A man in pyjamas and a postman's cap opens the door. "Day off," he explains. "Hina! Your delivery is here. The delivery is a boy."
Mr. Hayase squints at you. "Asagiri. I deliver to your aunt's shop. Letters from Tokyo. Your dad doesn't write much, does he." He calls upstairs.
"Wednesday's my day off. And on my day off a boy rings my bell at seven forty." He sighs, smiling. "HINA."
"Morning. One thing, kid. If she gives you a letter, you deliver it. By hand. That's the family rule."

ring_parent: "Toru-kun, if she asks you to read her stories online, say they're good. They ARE good. She won't believe me." Mrs. Hayase covers her mouth. "Oops."
"You're the boy in the photo on her desk! Oh, she'll kill me. HINA, IT'S THE PHOTO BOY."
parent_about_you: "Every summer you two ran up and down this street till the lanterns came on. Then you stopped coming. She waited by the station for two years."
"She's sharp, my Hina. Too sharp. Sharp people get lonely. Thank you for coming by."
"Her father says she's like him: things have to arrive. People too."
"She writes and writes up there. Sometimes I hear her laugh at what she's written. Sometimes she cries. Writers."
"If she gets too pushy, tell her. She'll pout, but she'll listen. She always listens to you."
"That shrine boy with the hood came by and bought a single white flower. Didn't say who for. Strange child. Sweet, though."
"You look like your grandfather when you frown. He bought chrysanthemums here every week."
"Come for dinner one day. She'll pretend she doesn't want you to. She'll set your place first."
parent_left: "Oh! She's gone, Toru-kun. Left at five to eight like a train. Run, you'll catch her by the lamp post."
"She left already. She looked at the street for a long time first. I think she was waiting for someone."
"Gone, gone. If you hurry you'll see her taking a photo of the same lamp post. Every day. I don't ask."
"You've missed her. She took an extra strawberry milk. Hm. I wonder who that was for."
"She's on her way. Here, take her the umbrella she forgot. By hand, mind. Family rule."
"She's gone to school early for the newspaper. Something about 'a scoop'. Everything is a scoop."
parent_evening: "She's upstairs writing. 'Don't disturb me, Mum, I'm in the middle of a chapter.' Chapter of what, I ask. She shuts the door."
"Evening, Toru-kun! She's developing film in the bathroom. Nobody can use the bathroom. Come back tomorrow."
"Oh, she just got back. She's pretending she didn't see you from the window. Say goodnight from here. Loudly."
"She's helping close the shop. Want to carry the buckets in? No? Ha. Goodnight, dear."
"It's Omagatoki, Toru-kun. Go home along the lit side. My husband says the post never goes out at this hour, and there's a reason."
"She's on the phone with somebody from the newspaper club. Or arguing with the Ura board again. Go home, it's getting dark."
come_out_low: Hina steps out, pushing her glasses up. "Fine. We're going the same way. Don't read anything into it."
"So you're walking with me. Okay. Rules: I ask questions, you answer them. Honestly."
"You really don't remember this street? The sunflowers? The ramune bottles? ...Nothing? Unbelievable."
She falls into step, already writing. "Time: seven fifty-five. Weather: wet. Subject: confused."
"Morning. I'll warn you, I talk fast. If you can't keep up, nod. You're good at nodding."
"I'm not walking with you because I want to. I'm walking with you because you're a story. Big difference."
"Hey. Wait. Turn round." Click. "Okay. Now we can go."
"I'm Hayase Hina. 2-C. Newspaper club. We've met. Many times. You were shorter."
come_out_mid: Hina comes out talking. "- and that's why the vending machine by the bridge is haunted. Oh. Morning. Where was I?"
"Ready! Let's walk fast. Not running fast. Thinking fast."
"Toru! I made a list of questions for our walk. Only twenty. Today's light."
She hands you a strawberry milk without looking. "For your brain. It needs help."
"Morning! You're less of a ghost today. Good. Ghosts are bad interviewees."
"Let's take the street with the lamp post. I need my photo. It's a series. Don't ask."
"Come on, slowpoke. You were always slow. You used to cry when I won races. You don't remember that either, huh."
"Walk on the shop side. The road side gets splashed. I learnt that the hard way. Many times."
come_out_high: Hina takes your sleeve for a moment, then lets go like it was an accident. "Morning. Let's go."
"You know what I like about mornings with you? I don't have to fill the silence. I still do. But I don't have to."
"Toru! I dreamed you remembered me. In the dream you said my old nickname. ...It was a good dream."
She smiles without the camera for once. "Okay. Today I'm off duty. Just walking."
"I brought two umbrellas. Then I left one at home on purpose. Don't analyse that."
"Morning! Your tie is crooked. Hold still." She fixes it in two seconds. "Better. Let's go."
"Every time you come to my door I feel ten years old. In a good way. Mostly."
"I've decided something. You don't have to remember. We'll just make new summers. Deal?"
come_out_rushed: Hina stumbles out with one sock in her hand. "You RANG. Mum said 'he's here' in her singing voice. I nearly died."
"Ten minutes early! Why? Is there news? Did something happen? Tell me on the way!"
"I haven't finished my hair! Don't look at my hair. Look at the sky. Look at the lamp post."
"You rang the bell! Mum is now going to tease me for a WEEK."
She shoves toast in her bag. "Breakfast is a social construct. Let's go."
"Early people are trustworthy, early people are trustworthy -" she repeats, putting her shoes on wrong.
"Toru! My film isn't loaded! I'll load it walking. Watch me. Don't watch me."
"You ruined my entrance. I had an entrance planned. Fine. Here's my exit. Let's go."
come_out_rain: Hina opens a clear umbrella. "Rain again. Fifteen days straight. That's not weather, that's a pattern."
"You notice it rains harder when the first-year in the hood looks sad? I'm writing it down. I'm not saying anything. I'm writing."
"Share? My umbrella's bigger. Don't make it weird. It's purely practical."
"Hold this so my camera doesn't get wet. Not me. The camera. Priorities."
"The flowers love it. Mum loves it. I hate it. My hair hates it more."
pickup_accept: "Fine! Together. But I'm interviewing you the whole way."
"Yes. Let's. Walk on my left, the camera's on my right."
"Okay! Like old times. You don't remember old times, but I'll narrate."
"Good. You can carry the newspaper drafts. They're heavy with truth."
"Deal. If anyone asks, I'm walking you. For an article."
"Let's go. If you see a rumour on the way, point at it. I'll destroy it."
pickup_decline: "Oh. You were just passing? ...Right. Of course. See you." She photographs the lamp post too hard.
"Hm. Okay. Then why did you ring? Never mind. I'll figure it out. I always do."
"Sure! Fine! I walk alone every day anyway. It's very efficient."
"Your loss. I had strawberry milk for you." She drinks it. Both of them.
"Okay. See you at school, Toru. Don't get lost."
walk: "Did you know the Ura board said you were a ghost? I posted a correction. They deleted it. Cowards."
"This lamp post. Every morning. Same angle. When I have a thousand photos I'll see what changes."
"My dad says there are letters in the post office nobody ever collects. He reads the addresses out loud so they don't feel forgotten."
"Strawberry milk is the most honest drink. It doesn't pretend to be healthy."
"Question one: what's your favourite colour? Question two: why? Question three: are you lying?"
"The fish shop man says the boats saw lights out at sea again. I need a photo. I need a boat. I need a braver boat."
"Makabe-sensei wrote 'insufficient evidence' on my essay. On my ESSAY. About my own grandmother."
"Hayate told me you snore in class. I'm not saying I believe him. I'm saying I wrote it down."
"You used to be scared of the crossroads with the six Jizo. You held my hand every time. ...You don't remember. Fine."
"The newspaper club has three members. Me, a boy who never comes, and a cactus."
"Rumours are like rain. Everyone gets wet and nobody remembers who started it."
"I'm writing an article about the accidents at school. Don't tell anyone. Especially not Shirasagi-senpai."
"I don't trust anything I didn't see myself. That's why I take so many photos. I see a lot."
"The station melody plays Toryanse. 'Going is easy, coming back is scary.' Who puts that in a station?"
"My mum puts a flower on the Jizo every morning. She says it's for the children who didn't come home."
"Have you noticed nobody in this town says 'goodbye'? They say 'see you later'. Even at funerals."
"Look! A cat on the roof. Click. Got it. That's the eighth cat this week. They're watching us."
"Reiji-senpai told me journalism is 'gossip in a tie'. I'm going to frame that and put it on his desk."
"I tried to interview Mio-senpai once. She answered every question with a ghost story. I got four articles out of it."
"Your aunt's mochi is the best in town. That's not opinion. I ran a survey. Of me."
"If you could print one true headline about yourself, what would it be? Mine: 'Girl Right Again'."
"My dad delivered a letter to an empty house once. The next day there was a reply in the box. He won't talk about it."
"The vending machine by the bridge gives you two drinks on rainy Thursdays. I have data."
"Why do you keep looking behind us? Is someone there? ...The hood kid? Again?"
"You know my camera is film? Every photo costs money. So I only photograph things that matter. Shut up."
"I hate when people whisper. If you've got something to say, say it in a headline."
"I memorised the bus timetable when I was eight. It hasn't changed since. Neither has this town."
"The sweet potato truck comes on Friday nights. Its song gets stuck in my head for days. Yaki-imooo."
"You've got a petal on your head. No, leave it. It suits you. Click."
"Do you believe in ghosts? Don't answer. I'll know from your face. ...Huh. Interesting face."
"My mum says you shouldn't give chrysanthemums unless someone died. So obviously I give them to Reiji-senpai."
"I once followed a stray cat for two hours to see where it went. It went to your aunt's shop."
"The Ura board has a thread about you. Don't read it. I read it. Don't worry. It's mostly wrong."
"The big hydrangeas by the crossroads change colour with the soil. Blue means acid. Pink means... I forget. Something."
"If you ever want to be in the paper, do something brave. Or stupid. Both sell."
"I've walked this road every day for ten years. With you it looks different. I don't know why. I'll find out."
"Hayate says he can smell rain coming. He can't. He just looks at the sky like everyone else."
"My grandpa was a fisherman. He said the sea never takes, it only borrows. I hated that. Still do."
"I'm trying a new thing: one compliment a day. Today's: your bag is a good colour. Done. That was hard."
"We used to bury bottle caps under the third cherry tree by the river. I bet they're still there. Want to dig?"
walk_close: "You really don't remember me. I remember everything. The sunflowers, the station, the day you left without saying bye. It's okay. I'm just saying it out loud once."
"I write stories. Online. Under another name. Don't look it up. ...If you look it up, don't tell me."
"The hero of my story walks the heroine to school. Every day. It's not about you. It's slightly about you."
"You're the only person I don't fact-check. I just believe you. That's weird for me."
"I'm scared of letters that don't arrive. Dad says it happens. I think it's the worst thing in the world."
"I dream I'm running all night with something to deliver. I never get there. Then I wake up and walk to school with you, and that's kind of the getting there."
"If something's wrong with the first-year in the hood, tell me. Not for the paper. For real."
"I kept your old ramune marble. From when we were seven. I'm not giving it back."
"Promise you'll tell me if you're leaving town again. Not a note. Not a text. By hand."
"Sometimes I think the town forgot something and is trying to remember it through us."
"I'm glad you came back. There. I said it. Don't put it in a headline."
"You know my nickname for you was 'Toro-chan'? Because you were slow like tuna. ...Don't laugh. You laughed! That's the same laugh!"
"If I ever write something that hurts you, tell me. I'll burn it. Even if it's true."
"Do you think we'd have been friends if you'd stayed? ...Yeah. Me too."
"I'm keeping a photo of every morning we walk. When it's a hundred, I'll show you. Not before."
walk_rain: "My shoes are full of water. My notebook is fine. Priorities."
"Rain this heavy and the post still goes out. My dad's out there right now. Respect."
"Move under the eaves. No, closer. Okay, not that close."
"Every drop is a fact nobody's checked. Okay, that's dramatic. It's very wet."
"Don't step in that puddle. Too late. Click. For the archive."
"If it keeps raining like this the river will flood the lower street. I'm writing to the council. Again."
arrive: "Made it. Seven minutes early. You're a good influence. Write that down. I'll write it down."
"School. Ugh. Back to being the girl with the camera. See you at lunch?"
"Thanks, Toru. That was... useful. For research. Okay, it was nice."
"I'm going to the club room. Don't follow me. Unless you want to. The cactus likes visitors."
"Here. Your umbrella. No, it's mine. Keep it. Bring it back tomorrow. By hand."
She photographs you at the gate. "Arrival documented. See you!"
"Shirasagi-senpai's watching. Act normal. You're bad at it. Go, go."
"Same time tomorrow? I'm only asking for the schedule. For accuracy."
ask_tell: "My schedule? Five to eight, out the shop door, past the lamp post, school by quarter past. You're going to come, aren't you. Mum will be unbearable."
"Seven fifty-five. Every day. I'm a train. Ring the bell - Mum'll answer, she'll ask you questions, don't answer any."
"Why should I - fine. Seven fifty-five. But if I see this on the Ura board I'll know it was you."
"You want to walk with me? On purpose? ...Seven fifty-five. Don't be late. I'll know."
"I leave at five to eight, I photograph the lamp post at seven fifty-seven, I'm at school at quarter past. There. Now you know more than my editor."
ask_refuse: "My schedule? Why? Who's asking? Is this for the Ura board? Is THIS how they get information?"
"No way. A journalist never reveals her movements. Or her sources. Or her breakfast."
"Ask me again when you remember my name from before. Not Hayase. The other one."
"You want to know where I am at what time? That's literally how stalkers start. ...Sorry. That came out wrong. Still no."
"Earn it. Bring me a real scoop and I'll tell you anything."
"Hmm." She studies you. "Not yet. Trust takes time. I'm documenting it."
home_offer: "Hey. You walking home? It's on my way. It's not. Shut up. Let's go."
"I'll walk you to Asagiri-do. I need to buy mochi anyway. For research."
"It's nearly Omagatoki. Mum says nobody should walk alone then. Come on."
"Walk with me? I'm doing a piece on the evening light. You're the scale reference."
"I'll take you home. You'll get lost otherwise. You always got lost. Every summer."
"Let's walk back together. I have nine more questions and they won't wait till tomorrow."
home_accept: "You want to walk me home? Oh. Okay. Mum's going to see. She's going to SEE."
"Sure! You can help carry a bucket of chrysanthemums upstairs. Kidding. Mostly."
"Okay. But the long way. Past the river. The light's good."
"Walk me home? Like when we were kids. ...You walked me home every day that summer. You don't remember. Let's go."
"Fine. But no photos. Of me. I take the photos."
"Yes. Let's. I'll tell you the whole Ura board scandal on the way."
home_refuse: "Today? No, I've got the paper to lay out. And the cactus needs water. Next time."
"No, I've got to interview the station master. About the melody. It's important. To me."
"Nah, I'm fine. I've walked that street alone for ten years. I'm a professional."
"Hmm, not yet. People will talk. I hate it when people talk. I'm the one who talks."
"Ask me when we're closer. Like, strawberry-milk-sharing closer."
"Can't. Mum needs me in the shop. Wednesday's a big day for funeral flowers. Weird, I know."
home_walk: "The shopping street at five is the best. Every shop puts the lights on at a different time. It's like a slow wave."
"Yuyake Koyake at five o'clock. Every kid in town runs home on that song. We used to race it."
"Look at the river. Gold. I've got eighty photos of the river at this hour and none of them are right."
"I hate saying goodbye. Let's just stop walking at my door and nod. Very cool. Very professional."
"The crows go home to the shrine mountain at dusk. Mio-senpai says they're counting the town."
"Mum says Omagatoki is when you meet things that look like people. So if I start looking weird, run."
"I submitted my article today. Makabe-sensei said 'well researched'. I'm going to die happy."
"The lamps are coming on. Click. That's the one. No. That one. Ugh."
"You know what I'd write about today? 'Boy walks girl home. Nothing happens. It's nice.' Terrible headline. True though."
"Do you ever feel like the town's watching? Not in a bad way. Like a grandma at a window."
"I wish we'd had this when we were kids. We did have this when we were kids. You just don't have it. I have it for both of us."
"The ramen shop smells like that every evening. Gen-san's been making the same broth for thirty years."
"When I'm old I want to run a tiny newspaper that only prints good news. One page. Weekly."
"You're quiet today. Quiet's okay. I'll be loud for both of us."
"The hood kid was at the shrine steps again. Just sitting. Waiting. Is he waiting for you?"
"Pinky promise you'll read my next piece first. Before the editor. Before Mum. Before the cactus."
"I think I'll remember this walk. Not because anything happens. Because nothing does."
"Hey, look, the sky's pink. Okay I'm not taking a photo. I'm just looking. With you."
"If you hear someone call your name from behind at dusk, don't answer the first time. Old Suzunari rule. My dad swears by it."
"I'm glad it's you walking me. Hayate would talk about bread the whole way."
goodbye: "Here we are. Thanks for walking me. Mum is in the window. Wave. Don't wave. Too late."
"Goodnight, Toru. Get home before the lamps finish. That's a rule."
"Okay. Bye. Not bye. See you later. Suzunari doesn't say bye."
"Thanks. Really. Text me when you're home. A full sentence. With punctuation."
She photographs your back as you go. You hear the click. "For the archive!"
"Same time tomorrow? Don't answer. I'll be at the lamp post."
"Night! If you dream of sunflowers, tell me. That means you're remembering."
"Go straight home. No talking to things that look like people. Bye!"
"Goodnight, Toro-chan." She slams the door before you can answer.
amane_cut_in: Hina freezes mid-sentence. "...Oh. The first-year. Good morning. Have you been there long? How long? A rough estimate."
"Hello! Nekomori, right? 1-A? I'm doing a piece on - " He glares. "- on nothing. Nothing at all."
She leans to you: "He's been behind us since the lamp post. I have three photos. In all of them he's looking at you."
"You can walk with us. It's a public road. Facts are facts."
"Are you crying? It's raining harder. Is that you? Sorry. Journalist habit. Ignore me."
"I'm not stealing anybody! I'm walking! Walking is legal!"
Hina lowers her camera very slowly. "Okay. No photos. Truce?"
"He's got cat ears. Toru. TORU. He's got - no, he hasn't. I need more sleep."
"I'll go ahead, it's fine. I'm used to being the extra in someone else's story." She tries to smile.
"Nekomori-kun, I'm his friend from when we were seven. I was here first. That's just chronology."
offer_pickup: "Tomorrow I'm coming to get you. Asagiri-do is on the way. It's not. Don't fact-check me."
"Let me pick you up in the morning. I want to see if you still sleep with your mouth open. For accuracy."
"I'll come by your aunt's shop tomorrow. I need mochi for the newspaper club anyway. You can come too."
"Tomorrow, wait at your door. If you're not there I'll ring the bell like a postman. Twice."
"I used to come get you every summer morning. Let me do it again. Tomorrow. Just to see."
"You keep getting to my door first. Tomorrow it's my turn. Deal?"
at_your_door: Hina is at the sweet shop door, talking to your aunt at double speed. "- and then he - oh! Morning! Let's go!"
"I came! I'm early. I'm never early. Don't make a big deal. Okay, make a small deal."
She's photographing the Asagiri-do sign. "It hasn't changed in ten years. You have. A bit. Ready?"
"Your aunt gave me tea. She says you used to hide under the counter when I came. Interesting. Let's go."
"Morning! I brought strawberry milk. Two. Don't make that face. You love it."
"Pick-up as promised. By hand. Hayase family rule. Come on!"
promise_yes: "Tomorrow? Same time? ...Okay. Put it in your calendar. I'm putting it in mine. In pen."
"A promise? You'll keep it? People don't, you know. But you will. I've decided."
"Fine. Tomorrow. If you're late I'll write an article about it."
"Pinky swear. By hand. Okay. I'm holding you to this."
promise_broken: "You didn't come. I waited at the lamp post for fifteen minutes. I took fifteen photos of an empty street. Thanks."
"You said you'd come. You know what my dad says about things that don't arrive? He doesn't say anything. He just looks sad."
"It's fine. I'm writing it down. Not to be mean. So I remember not to wait next time."
"You left without saying bye once. Ten years ago. Don't make it a habit."

Mon: "Monday. The Ura board is always worst on Mondays. Let's not look."
Tue: "Tuesday. Newspaper deadline. If I'm grumpy, it's not you. It's the deadline."
Wed: "Wednesday! Dad's day off. Did he answer the door in pyjamas? He always does."
Thu: "Thursday. Rainy-Thursday vending machine day. Two drinks. Science."
